claims.text: Adjusting element combinations and proportions can optimize the chemical composition of high-entropy alloys.
Chemical-composition optimization alters chemical short-range order and ordered clusters in high-entropy alloys.
Optimized chemical composition produces improved microstructures in high-entropy alloys.
The resulting microstructures enhance the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
The resulting microstructures enhance the thermal stability of high-entropy alloys.
The resulting microstructures enhance the radiation-damage resistance of high-entropy alloys.
Composition-optimized high-entropy alloys have superior comprehensive performance relative to non-optimized high-entropy alloys.
Composition-optimized high-entropy alloys are suitable for high-temperature operation.
Composition-optimized high-entropy alloys are suitable for extreme irradiation environments.
Composition-optimized high-entropy alloys are suitable for lightweight applications.
Selective laser melting, arc melting, and laser powder bed fusion can be used to investigate composition-dependent properties of high-entropy alloys.
